title: Logical Reasoning
description: Class 9 IMO — Logical Reasoning: number and letter series, advanced coding-decoding, direction and distance, blood relations, three-set Venn diagrams, dice and cubes, and calendar and clock problems.

topics.title: Series and Coding–Decoding
topics.concept:
In a number or letter series, find the rule linking consecutive terms — a constant difference, a ratio, squares/cubes, or alternating patterns — then extend it.

In coding–decoding, letters or digits are shifted or substituted by a rule (for example +1 in the alphabet); discover the rule from the given pair and apply it to the new word.

examples.solution: Differences 4, 6, 8 grow by 2, so next gap is 10 → 30.
Each letter moves +1: D→E, O→P, G→H, giving EPH.

recap: Series: spot the rule (difference, ratio, squares) and extend.
Coding: find the shift/substitution from the example, then apply it.

quiz.q: In the sequence P₁ = √3, P₂ = √12, P₃ = √27, P₄ = √48, the next term P₅ is:
quiz.explanation: The terms are 1√3, 2√3, 3√3, 4√3, so the next is 5√3 = √(25 × 3) = √75.

quiz.q: Find the next term in the pattern of interior angles of a regular polygon with n sides, starting from n = 3, 4, 5... If a quadrilateral has three acute angles each equal to 75°, what is the logical value of its fourth angle?
quiz.explanation: Sum of angles of a quadrilateral is 360°. Sum of three angles = 75° + 75° + 75° = 225°. Fourth angle = 360° − 225° = 135°.

topics.title: Direction, Distance and Blood Relations
topics.concept:
Direction and distance problems track movements (turns are left/right relative to facing); sketch each step and use Pythagoras for the straight-line distance from start to finish.

Blood relations are solved by drawing a small family tree from the clues and reading off the required relationship.

examples.problem: Walk 3 km East then 4 km North. Distance from start?
A's mother is B's sister. How is B related to A?
examples.solution: B is A's aunt (mother's sister) or uncle — B is A's aunt.

recap: Sketch directions; straight-line gap via Pythagoras.
Draw a family tree to decode blood relations.

quiz.q: In a logical sequence of figures, the first circle is divided into 2 sectors, the second into 4 sectors, and the third into 8 sectors. Following this pattern, how many sectors will the fifth circle have?
quiz.explanation: The number of sectors follows the pattern 2¹, 2², 2³. The fourth circle will have 2⁴ = 16. The fifth circle will have 2⁵ = 32.

quiz.q: Find the missing term in the sequence: 2, √5, √6, √7, 2√2, …
quiz.explanation: Writing each term under a root: √4, √5, √6, √7, √8. The next term is √9 = 3.

topics.title: Venn Diagrams, Dice and Calendar/Clock
topics.concept:
Three-set Venn diagrams show overlaps; the central region belongs to all three sets. Dice and cube problems use the fact that opposite faces of a standard die total 7, and a painted cube cut into smaller cubes has predictable painted-face counts.

Clock: the minute hand moves 6° per minute, the hour hand 0.5° per minute. Calendar: each ordinary year shifts the weekday by 1, a leap year by 2.

examples.solution: The hour hand is at 90° from 12, the minute at 0°, so 90°.

examples.problem: A die shows 2 on top. What is on the bottom?

recap: Venn centre = common to all three sets; opposite die faces sum to 7.
Minute hand 6°/min, hour hand 0.5°/min; ordinary year shifts weekday by 1.

quiz.q: In a histogram, the width of the rectangles is proportional to:
quiz.explanation: The width of a rectangle in a histogram corresponds to the size of the class interval on the x-axis.

quiz.q: In a logical diagram, if a rectangle has its diagonals intersecting at point O such that angle BOC = 60°, what is the value of angle OAD?
quiz.explanation: In a rectangle, diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so OA = OB = OC = OD. Angle AOD = angle BOC = 60° (vertically opposite). In triangle AOD, OA = OD, which implies angle OAD = angle ODA. Since angle AOD = 60°, angle OAD + angle ODA = 180° − 60° = 120° → angle OAD = 60°.

questions.q: A card is selected from a standard deck. What is the probability it is a red king?
questions.explanation: There are 2 red kings (King of Hearts, King of Diamonds). Probability = 2/52 = 1/26.

questions.q: Which graph is most suitable to represent continuous grouped frequency distribution?
questions.explanation: A histogram is used to represent a continuous grouped frequency distribution because there are no gaps between the class intervals.

questions.q: Which of the following conditions is NOT sufficient to prove that two lines intersected by a transversal are parallel?
options: The sum of any two interior angles is 180°
A pair of alternate interior angles are equal
A pair of corresponding angles are equal
A pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal are supplementary
questions.explanation: The sum of ANY two random interior angles being 180° is meaningless unless they are specifically consecutive interior angles on the same side of the transversal.

questions.q: Rays OC and OE lie above a straight line AB through point O, dividing the straight angle into three parts: ∠AOC = 3y, ∠COE = y and ∠EOB = 2y. Find the value of y.
questions.explanation: The three angles on the straight line AB add up to 180°: 3y + y + 2y = 180° → 6y = 180° → y = 30°.

questions.q: Two cubes each of volume 64 cm³ are joined end to end. The surface area of the resulting cuboid is:
questions.explanation: Volume of one cube = 64 cm³ → side a = 4 cm. When joined, length of cuboid l = 4+4 = 8 cm, breadth b = 4 cm, height h = 4 cm. TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) = 2(32 + 16 + 32) = 2(80) = 160 cm².

questions.q: Diagonals AC and BD of a trapezium ABCD with AB || DC intersect each other at O. Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: Triangles ABD and ABC are on same base AB and between same parallels. Area(ABD) = Area(ABC). Subtracting Area(AOB) gives Area(AOD) = Area(BOC).

questions.q: In a certain code, 'PARALLELOGRAM' is related to 'OPPOSITE_SIDES_EQUAL'. If we analyze the properties of a rhombus, which of the following logical pairs represents its unique diagonal property?
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a special parallelogram whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°). Thus, 'BISECT_AT_RIGHT_ANGLES' is the correct logical property.

questions.q: If 5 points are marked on the circumference of a circle, what is the total number of unique chords that can be drawn joining these points?
questions.explanation: Choosing any 2 points out of 5 creates a chord. This is combinations: 5C2 = (5 × 4) / 2 = 10.

questions.q: If every side of a triangle is doubled, the ratio of the area of the original triangle to the new triangle is:
questions.explanation: When sides are doubled, the semi-perimeter doubles, making each (s-a) term double. √(2s × 2(s-a) × 2(s-b) × 2(s-c)) = √16 × Area = 4 × Area. Ratio is 1:4.

questions.q: Points A and B have coordinates that satisfy y = 3x − 5. If the x-coordinate of A increases by 4 units to become the x-coordinate of B, by how many units does the y-coordinate increase?
questions.explanation: Let A be (x, 3x − 5). If x increases by 4, the new x-coordinate is x + 4. The new y-coordinate is 3(x + 4) − 5 = 3x + 12 − 5 = (3x − 5) + 12. Thus, the y-coordinate increases by exactly 12 units.

questions.q: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 12 cm, and 13 cm. The altitude drawn on the longest side is:
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 cm². Also, ½ × 13 × altitude = 30 → altitude = 60/13 cm.

questions.q: If a line segment AB is parallel to another line segment CD, and O is the midpoint of AD, then any line segment passing through O and terminating at AB and CD will be bisected at O. This logical step relies directly on which pair of angles?
options: Alternate interior angles and vertically opposite angles
questions.explanation: To prove the triangles formed are congruent (which shows the segment is bisected), we use alternate interior angles (since AB || CD) and vertically opposite angles at O.

questions.q: An angle tracking device notes that in a trapezium ABCD with AB parallel to CD, angle A = 50° and angle B = 70°. What are the values of angle D and angle C respectively?
questions.explanation: Since AB || CD, adjacent angles on the same transverse side are supplementary. Angle A + angle D = 180° → 50° + angle D = 180° → angle D = 130°. Angle B + angle C = 180° → 70° + angle C = 180° → angle C = 110°.

questions.q: The probability of a sure (or certain) event is:
questions.explanation: A sure event always happens. The number of favourable outcomes equals the total number of outcomes, making the probability 1.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Two triangles having the same base and equal areas will have their corresponding altitudes equal.
Reason (R): Area of a triangle = ½ × base × altitude.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Since Area = ½ × b × h, if Area and base (b) are constant, the altitude (h) must also be equal. The reason correctly explains the assertion.
